title: Atomic multi-op records: one checksummed frame, plus a versioned log header
description: Crash and replication atomicity for a multi-operation unit comes from making it ONE checksummed record (one frame, one offset) and ONE replication command, not from writing its frames contiguously. A new record kind needs a format version: magic+version header for new files, headerless files read as legacy and upgraded via temp+fsync+rename, newer versions refuse startup naming both versions; append enum variants at the end. Test the legacy path with a fixture from an independent encoder.
whenToUse: Multi-operation units that must survive a crash or dropped connection all-or-nothing; on-disk format changes old binaries cannot read.
whenNotToUse: Single-operation writes; files rewritten atomically as a whole (snapshots).
